title: AMD Buys Li Fei-Fei’s World Labs For $8.2bn
key_facts: AMD said it would buy World Labs, the start-up of AI researcher Li Fei-Fei, for $8.2 billion (£6.2bn) in stock.
Li, a Stanford professor who has worked at Google, will become chief scientist and an executive vice-president at AMD.
World Labs was founded two years ago to research AI that interacts with the physical world; its models help train AI agents or physical devices in physical environments.
At a presentation earlier this year Li and AMD chief executive Lisa Su showed a World Labs model called Marble creating a three-dimensional environment from several images.
AMD is one of the main rivals to Nvidia in GPUs used to speed up AI workloads, and is a previous investor in World Labs, as is Nvidia.
The article ties the deal to Nvidia's September agreement to buy Hugging Face for $12.9bn.
quote_evidence: Renowned AI researcher Li Fei-Fei is to become chief scientist and an executive vice-president at AMD after the chipmaker said it would buy Li’s start-up World Labs for $8.2 billion (£6.2bn) in stock.
The company is a previous investor in World Labs, as is Nvidia.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading chip maker is buying a top research lab for AI that works with physical space, and hiring its founder.
notes: Single outlet read; AMD is quoted as the announcer. No closing date or approvals in the text.
